items.stem: Historians overwhelmingly identify what as the central cause of the Civil War?

options.text: Conflict over the expansion and future of slavery
options.rationale: Correct: the sectional crisis turned on slavery's extension into the territories.
This was not a national dividing issue.

options.text: A dispute over the national anthem

options.rationale: A minor technical matter, not the cause of war.

items.explanation: Correct: the sectional crisis turned on slavery's extension into the territories.

items.stem: Which TWO were direct constitutional or legal outcomes of the Civil War and Reconstruction? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The abolition of slavery by the Thirteenth Amendment
options.rationale: Correct: the Thirteenth Amendment ended legal slavery.

options.text: Birthright citizenship and equal protection under the Fourteenth Amendment
options.rationale: Correct: the Fourteenth Amendment established these principles.

options.text: The creation of the Federal Reserve
options.rationale: The Federal Reserve was established in 1913, unrelated to Reconstruction.
That came with the Seventeenth Amendment in 1913.

items.explanation: Correct: the Thirteenth Amendment ended legal slavery.

items.stem: Why is 'the civil rights movement was the work of one leader' a misleading summary?

options.text: It depended on many organisations, local organisers and sustained grassroots action over decades
options.rationale: Correct: the movement was broad, decentralised and long, not the work of one figure.

options.text: Because there were no national leaders at all
options.rationale: There were prominent leaders; the error is crediting only one.
It produced major legislation; the error is about who made it happen.

options.text: Because it occurred entirely in one city

items.explanation: Correct: the movement was broad, decentralised and long, not the work of one figure.
